requirements.RPT-MODEL-001: The model carries all sixteen ICH E3 top-level sections, numbered 1 to 16, with E3's own headings.
requirements.RPT-MODEL-002: The Section 14 substructure reproduces E3: 14.1 demographic, 14.2 efficacy, 14.3 safety, and 14.3.1 to 14.3.4 (AE displays, death and SAE listings, narratives, abnormal laboratory listings). 14.3.3 is modelled as prose, because in E3 it is.
requirements.RPT-MODEL-003: Section 16 carries the full appendix structure: 16.1.1 to 16.1.12, 16.2.1 to 16.2.8, 16.3.1 to 16.3.2 and 16.4.
requirements.RPT-MODEL-004: Section 16.1.9 (Documentation of Statistical Methods) is declared as accepting generated provenance content — the slot E3 reserved in 1995 that open.csr fills mechanically.
requirements.RPT-MODEL-005: Section numbers and slugs are each unique, every number is well formed, and every subsection names a parent that exists in the model.
requirements.RPT-MODEL-006: Every declared content type comes from the closed vocabulary `text`, `in_text_display`, `post_text_index`, `generated_provenance`; a structural heading declares none.
requirements.RPT-MODEL-007: Section level, parent and document ordering are derived from the dotted number, so 9.10 sorts after 9.2 and no ordering metadata is stored redundantly.
requirements.RPT-ASM-001: Every slot targets a section that exists in the document model and that accepts the content the slot supplies.
requirements.RPT-ASM-002: Every text block named by a slot exists in the Text Library.
requirements.RPT-ASM-003: Section 14 display numbers are assigned from `post_text` order at build time and appear nowhere in the source; reordering a slot renumbers the displays without touching a slug.
requirements.RPT-ASM-004: An assigned display number that would collide with a section number in the document model fails the build, because such a collision makes every cross-reference in the document ambiguous.
requirements.RPT-ASM-005: A display may occupy at most one post-text position, and no two displays may be assigned the same number.
requirements.RPT-ASM-006: A slot naming an unknown section, an unknown text block, or content the section does not accept is rejected with the reason.
requirements.RPT-ASM-007: The demonstration assembly claims only the sections it populates, names the study, its data cut-off and its analysis set, and states its scope limits — including the absence of efficacy data (design D12).
requirements.RPT-ASM-008: The assembler places `in_text` display variants in narrative sections and `post_text` variants only under Section 14, and assigns each post-text display its derived number.
requirements.RPT-ASM-009: A display placed both in-text and post-text renders both variants from the same ARD file — one analysis, two renderings, never re-authored.
requirements.RPT-ARD-001: Every display in the assembly resolves to a real ARD — the pipeline output pointed at by `outputs/<slug>/current.json` where one exists, a committed fixture otherwise — and the assembled document records which, so a report built from fixtures can never be mistaken for one built from a pipeline run.
requirements.RPT-PROV-001: Section 16.1.9 is generated from the provenance envelope of every ARD in the report: specification and display hashes, input dataset hashes with row counts and source package versions, the R and package versions, and the source commit. It is generated, never authored.
requirements.RPT-OUT-001: `assemble()` emits `docs/assembled/csr.json` in the documented `opencsr/csr/v1` shape: study, template, flat sections, display index, text blocks, provenance appendix and gate report.
requirements.RPT-OUT-002: The section list is flat and in document order, and every section that names a parent names one that is present — the site builder can nest it without a second pass.
requirements.RPT-OUT-003: A build with any structural error, unresolved binding, unresolved cross-reference or numeric-fidelity violation reports `ok: false` and exits non-zero; the shipped configuration builds clean.
requirements.RPT-OUT-004: The assembled document contains the full E3 skeleton, with sections the demonstration does not fill marked unpopulated rather than dropped — the numbering is what makes the artifact recognisable as a CSR.
requirements.RPT-OUT-005: `docs/assembled/csr.html` contains resolved values and never a raw binding token or an unresolved marker.
requirements.RPT-OUT-006: `csr.html` is self-contained: no external host, no script, no external stylesheet, no font or image fetched at view time.
requirements.RPT-OUT-007: The rendered document shows the assigned display numbering, the per-block gate report and the generated provenance appendix, so a reader can see the evidence for the numbers beside them.

rows.text: The model carries all sixteen ICH E3 top-level sections, numbered 1 to 16, with E3's own headings.

The Section 14 substructure reproduces E3: 14.1 demographic, 14.2 efficacy, 14.3 safety, and 14.3.1 to 14.3.4 (AE displays, death and SAE listings, narratives, abnormal laboratory listings). 14.3.3 is modelled as prose, because in E3 it is.
Section 16 carries the full appendix structure: 16.1.1 to 16.1.12, 16.2.1 to 16.2.8, 16.3.1 to 16.3.2 and 16.4.
Section 16.1.9 (Documentation of Statistical Methods) is declared as accepting generated provenance content — the slot E3 reserved in 1995 that open.csr fills mechanically.
Section numbers and slugs are each unique, every number is well formed, and every subsection names a parent that exists in the model.
Every declared content type comes from the closed vocabulary `text`, `in_text_display`, `post_text_index`, `generated_provenance`; a structural heading declares none.
Section level, parent and document ordering are derived from the dotted number, so 9.10 sorts after 9.2 and no ordering metadata is stored redundantly.
Every slot targets a section that exists in the document model and that accepts the content the slot supplies.
Every text block named by a slot exists in the Text Library.
Section 14 display numbers are assigned from `post_text` order at build time and appear nowhere in the source; reordering a slot renumbers the displays without touching a slug.
An assigned display number that would collide with a section number in the document model fails the build, because such a collision makes every cross-reference in the document ambiguous.
A display may occupy at most one post-text position, and no two displays may be assigned the same number.
A slot naming an unknown section, an unknown text block, or content the section does not accept is rejected with the reason.

The demonstration assembly claims only the sections it populates, names the study, its data cut-off and its analysis set, and states its scope limits — including the absence of efficacy data (design D12).
The assembler places `in_text` display variants in narrative sections and `post_text` variants only under Section 14, and assigns each post-text display its derived number.
A display placed both in-text and post-text renders both variants from the same ARD file — one analysis, two renderings, never re-authored.

Every display in the assembly resolves to a real ARD — the pipeline output pointed at by `outputs/<slug>/current.json` where one exists, a committed fixture otherwise — and the assembled document records which, so a report built from fixtures can never be mistaken for one built from a pipeline run.

Section 16.1.9 is generated from the provenance envelope of every ARD in the report: specification and display hashes, input dataset hashes with row counts and source package versions, the R and package versions, and the source commit. It is generated, never authored.
`assemble()` emits `docs/assembled/csr.json` in the documented `opencsr/csr/v1` shape: study, template, flat sections, display index, text blocks, provenance appendix and gate report.
The section list is flat and in document order, and every section that names a parent names one that is present — the site builder can nest it without a second pass.
A build with any structural error, unresolved binding, unresolved cross-reference or numeric-fidelity violation reports `ok: false` and exits non-zero; the shipped configuration builds clean.

The assembled document contains the full E3 skeleton, with sections the demonstration does not fill marked unpopulated rather than dropped — the numbering is what makes the artifact recognisable as a CSR.
`docs/assembled/csr.html` contains resolved values and never a raw binding token or an unresolved marker.
`csr.html` is self-contained: no external host, no script, no external stylesheet, no font or image fetched at view time.
The rendered document shows the assigned display numbering, the per-block gate report and the generated provenance appendix, so a reader can see the evidence for the numbers beside them.
